name: Lakebound — The Great Lakes Multicultural Music Festival
creator: Lakebound Collective (independent, est. 2188)
description: A four-day annual music festival held on the reclaimed lakefront between Meridian's Tier 2 and Tier 3 zones, deliberately designed with sliding-scale admission to draw audiences from Tiers 1 through 4 into shared physical space. The festival's programming philosophy treats all musical lineages as equally present and equally recombinant — a single stage might move from Carnatic-derived synthesizer ragas to Afro-diasporic polyrhythm ensembles to Appalachian drone electronics within an hour. Neural feed broadcast rights are sold to fund free Tier 1 access.
medium: physical attendance, neural feed broadcast, BCI-synced haptic audio experience
cultural_impact: Lakebound is the most attended annual live music event in GLMZ and one of the few spaces where bodies from different tiers genuinely share ground — its reputation as a site of cross-tier encounter makes it symbolically and politically significant far beyond music.
controversy: A 2215 incident in which Tier 4 attendees in a premium zone were given BCI-boosted audio that Tier 1 attendees couldn't access caused a major schism in the organizing collective and nearly ended the festival.
story_hooks: The 2226 Lakebound headliner is a neural-feed music collective from the Gray Zone whose members have never performed physically before — and someone has sent threats suggesting one of them shouldn't make it to the stage.
A Tier 1 attendee at Lakebound using a borrowed BCI rig accidentally intercepts a private communication between two Tier 4 attendees that implicates a corponation in the 2179 Surge.

The sliding-scale admission system has been quietly manipulated for three years to extract data profiles on Tier 1 and 2 attendees — and the person who set it up is standing in the festival crowd right now.
